title: Gorilla Emoji 🦍 Meaning: Strength, Apes and Gym Energy
description: The 🦍 gorilla emoji means raw strength, gym energy and the 'apes together strong' meme. Learn its uses in fitness, investing slang and wildlife, plus pitfalls.
summary: The 🦍 gorilla emoji shows a dark, powerful great ape. People use it for brute strength and gym motivation, for acting wild or primal, for the apes together strong meme from retail investing forums, and for real gorillas in zoos and wildlife conservation.
meaning: Strength comes first. A gorilla can lift and tear far beyond a human, so 🦍 is shorthand for raw power. Lifters post it with heavy deadlifts, sports fans use it for a dominant player, and friends call someone a gorilla when they carried a couch up the stairs alone. It is cruder and louder than the biceps emoji, closer to chest-thumping.

It also stands for going primal. Eating a huge meal with no manners, yelling at a game or abandoning sophistication for pure instinct can all be described with a gorilla. The tone is self-mocking: the sender is admitting to caveman behavior and enjoying it, the way someone might beat their chest after a big win.

In early 2021, retail investors on the WallStreetBets forum began calling themselves apes during the GameStop stock surge, borrowing the line apes together strong from the Planet of the Apes films. The gorilla emoji, often next to diamond hands, became a badge of that crowd and still appears in meme-stock talk.

Literal uses matter too. Gorillas are endangered great apes, and zoo visitors, documentary fans and conservation groups use 🦍 for them. Harambe, the gorilla killed at the Cincinnati Zoo in 2016, became a long-running internet meme, and the emoji still turns up in references to him, from tribute posts to absurdist jokes.

contexts.label: In fitness
contexts.body: Gym check-ins, personal records and pre-workout hype get the gorilla. It suggests heavy, primal strength rather than toned elegance. Training partners use it to egg each other on, and some lifting communities adopt it as a mascot for unapologetic power.

contexts.label: In investing slang
contexts.body: In meme-stock communities, ape means a retail investor who holds stubbornly together with others. The gorilla often pairs with gem and hands emojis or a rocket. Outside those circles the reference can be lost, so it reads as either a joke or a sign of membership.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Friends call someone a gorilla for strength or for chaotic, loud behavior. It can describe a hungry person devouring food or a sports fan roaring at the TV. Used at oneself it is funny; aimed at someone else, context decides whether it is praise or a jab.

confusedWith.difference: 🦧 is the orangutan, a reddish-orange ape with a gentler, more contemplative image. 🦍 is dark and muscular and stands for power. People choose the orangutan for chill or goofy moods and the gorilla for strength.
🐵 is a cartoon monkey face used for playful, cheeky moods. The gorilla is a full great ape and much heavier in tone. Monkeys mean mischief; gorillas mean muscle.
💪 is the standard emoji for strength and effort, usable in any setting. 🦍 is louder and more primal, suggesting brute force and chest-thumping energy rather than polite encouragement.

avoid: Never use ape or gorilla imagery to describe a person's race; it has a long history as a racist slur.
Avoid it in professional settings, where it can come across as crude or aggressive.
design: A dark gray or black gorilla, usually drawn as a head and upper body or in a seated pose, with a prominent brow, broad chest and powerful arms. Some designs show a grumpy expression. It was added in 2016 and does not support skin tone modifiers.

faqs.q: What does 🦍 mean in the stock market?
faqs.a: It refers to apes, the name retail investors on WallStreetBets adopted during the 2021 GameStop rally. Apes together strong means holding shares as a group. It often appears with 💎🙌 and 🚀.

faqs.q: What does 🦍 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: Usually he feels strong, has been working out, or is joking about acting primal. In group chats it can praise a friend's strength. It is rarely romantic, though some use it to flex jokingly.
On its own, no. It becomes offensive when used to describe people of a particular race, a long-standing racist trope. In fitness, investing or wildlife contexts it is ordinary.
🦍 is the gorilla, dark and muscular, used for strength. 🦧 is the orangutan, orange and calmer, often used for thoughtful or goofy moods..
